question: At frozen compact interpreter revision, what are request costs, finite mixed-window tails, suspended physical memory and retained code costs on one Linux x86_64 WSL host?
corpus: fixtures/common_{scalar,weighted,stateful}.py byte-identical for primary and ordinary Python arms; fixture reference is handwritten lower bound; old Pysolate adapter separate

prepared_owner.scope: Separate counting-allocator diagnostic, includes compiler scratch retained by runtime; logical interpreter ownership bytes and native machine-code bytes have distinct definitions

controls: serial arms, taskset CPU 2, no parallel experiments; native uninstrumented speed binary and separate counting allocator diagnostic binary; fresh process per command and per memory cell; process startup/stdlib import excluded in resident rows, separately observed; spawn includes child startup and teardown, fork includes child lifecycle; prepared source code excluded explicitly
statistics: per-round means and ranges; pooled request wall median; nearest-rank short-task p50/p95/p99; batch CPU counted once, no per-request invented CPU; finite-window throughput and overload counts; memory per independent process mean/range, PSS and RSS distinct
limitations: synthetic bounded success corpus, ordinary Python arithmetic and authority differ; WSL hypervisor and uncontrolled Windows activity; explicit warmup counts do not establish PyPy JIT equilibrium; no single mixed ranking across unmatched lifecycle/representation arms
storage: all targets, downloads and raw JSONL remain WSL; commit only plan, identities, summaries, reproducible scripts and report
